title: Log and Graph Compression Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Record Store
ClickHouse
Neo4j
Summary Vertices
Capacity Planning
description: A Chart.js lab that uses the LRS design document's published estimates to compare ClickHouse rows with summary vertices over a semester, and graph writes per second with and without summary vertices as the ingest rate and sync cadence change.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: How summary vertices decouple the graph write rate from the ingest rate
learningObjectives: The learner will examine how summary vertices decouple graph write rate from ingest rate, using the design's published estimates as inputs.
prerequisites: The roles of ClickHouse and the Neo4j graph in the full LRS (Chapter 20)
The six summary vertices and their grains (Chapter 20)

accessibility.notes: Each canvas has an aria-label that is rewritten with the current values; controls are labeled native inputs; the note panel is an aria-live region; bar values are printed on the chart

controls.label: Ingest rate
controls.purpose: Raise the rate for the same student population (a burst)

controls.label: Sync cadence
controls.purpose: Length of the summarizer's sync window

controls.label: Grain
controls.purpose: Choose the summary vertex for the semester bar chart

controls.label: Show design estimates
controls.purpose: Overlay the design's 5 s, 60 s and 300 s rows

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Examine a model built from published estimates by varying its inputs
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Slider exploration with an overlay of the source's own data points and hover arithmetic
keyQuestions: Why does a 5x burst barely change the summary write rate?
What does a longer sync cadence trade for fewer upserts?
Which grain compresses least, and why?
commonMisconceptions: Graph writes must scale with the statement rate
Storage compression and write-rate compression are the same ratio
assessmentOpportunities: Ratio-of-change comparison for the two lines under a burst
Labeling which numbers are design estimates and which are interpolated

simulation.modelType: Analytical model from published design estimates
equations: semester rows = rate x 0.40 x 36,000 s x 90 days
one vertex per statement: writes/s = rate x 5 (vertex + ~4 edges)
summary upserts/s = min(rate x cadence, 100,000 x 1.5 x (cadence/60)^0.437) / cadence
assumptions: Design section 4 and 4.1 estimates are used as inputs
The active student population is fixed at ~100,000, so higher rates are bursts
A 90-day semester is half the design's 180-day year
limitations: All values are design estimates, not measurements
Values between the design's three cadence rows are this sim's interpolation
The design gives no storage ratio for LearningSession
